input_files: northline_invoices_sept_2026.csv - the carrier's September freight bills, one line per bill, with pro number, dates, billed weight and class, base charge, discount, net linehaul, fuel surcharge percent and amount, accessorials and total

bills_of_lading_sept_2026.csv - the shipper's bills of lading behind the September freight bills, with pro number, pickup date, consignee, product group, pieces, declared weight, the accessorial services requested and the delivery date

northline_contract_2026.docx - the pricing sections of the motor carrier agreement: rating, deficit weight, class, discount and minimum, reweigh, rounding, fuel surcharge, accessorials, duplicate and corrected bills, claims and undercharges

northline_contract_rates_2026.xlsx - the contract tariff exhibit: lane rates by destination state and weight break, class factors and product group classes, accessorial schedule, discount and minimum, fuel surcharge table

northline_fuel_bulletin_sept_2026.docx - the carrier's monthly fuel bulletin with the DOE diesel index for each Monday of the quarter and the surcharge percentage it printed for the week, and how the index is applied

northline_billing_file_sept_2026.docx - Northline revenue accounting's transmittal listing the documents held in its billing file behind the September freight bills, with the particulars shown on each document
shipping_desk_correspondence_sept_2026.docx - the Halvorsen shipping desk's email correspondence with Northline customer service and pricing for September, printed for the audit file
output_files: northline_audit_sept2026.xlsx - the freight audit workbook with the summary, the line-by-line rating against the contract, the exceptions, the claim schedule, the undercharge list and the note to the controller
task_instruction:
Northline's September freight bills are sitting in accounts payable, and Ingrid will not release them until someone has audited them against the contract. I'm the distribution manager at Halvorsen Building Products in Fargo, North Dakota, and the carrier audit has been mine since we signed the Northline agreement. Ingrid Solheim is our controller, and she files the overcharge claims, so what she needs from me is a worked audit she can send to Northline's claims desk without reworking it. I am out at the Bismarck yard through the middle of the month, and you have audited LTL freight bills before, so I am handing you the September file: northline_invoices_sept_2026.csv, bills_of_lading_sept_2026.csv, northline_contract_2026.docx, northline_contract_rates_2026.xlsx, and northline_fuel_bulletin_sept_2026.docx. Northline's revenue accounting also sent over a listing of what sits in their billing file behind the September bills, northline_billing_file_sept_2026.docx, and I have printed the shipping desk's email traffic with Northline for the month, shipping_desk_correspondence_sept_2026.docx.

Build the audit as one workbook named northline_audit_sept2026.xlsx. The first tab is the summary Ingrid reads: what Northline billed for the month, what the contract says we owe, the difference, how many bills carry an exception and of what kinds, and what we are claiming. Behind it I want every freight bill rated under the contract line by line beside what Northline billed, the exceptions called out with the contract term each one rests on, and a claim schedule in the form the agreement asks for that Ingrid can attach to the claim letter. Anything where Northline billed us less than the contract goes on its own list, reported and not netted. Put a note to Ingrid on the last tab with what she should know before she files, including anything in the file that the documents do not settle. I need the workbook by Friday, October 16.

rubric.description: The deliverable is a single workbook named exactly northline_audit_sept2026.xlsx whose first worksheet is the summary of the month's billings, the contract amount, the exceptions and the claim.
The summary's overcharges claimed reaches its value through a plain cell reference to the claim schedule's total behind it, or a sum over the same claim rows alike, standing at exactly $2,285.16.
The summary states the total billed by Northline as $24,704.54.
The summary states the total due under the contract as $22,591.56.
The corrected freight bill on the Hudson windows pro is rated as the live bill at $632.45 due.
The withdrawn Hudson windows freight bill is claimed at $650.74 as due at zero.
The Eau Claire roofing shipment is claimed at $113.93 under the deficit weight rule in section 4.2.
The Eau Claire windows shipment of 930 pounds is claimed at $32.43 at the 1M break minimum.
The Minot sealants shipment is claimed at $46.45 on the product group class of 85.
The Norfolk gypsum board shipment is rated at a net linehaul of $151.03 at the class 70 the signed inspection certificate supports.
The Glendive vinyl siding shipment is claimed at $31.96 at its bill of lading weight of 2,210 pounds.
The Miles City fasteners shipment is rated at $460.43 due at the 2M break on the certified ticket weight of 2,040 pounds.
The liftgate billed on the Detroit Lakes siding shipment is rated as due on the shipping desk's written confirmation of September 16.
The reconsignment charge of $110 on the Norfolk sealants shipment is rated as due on the shipping desk's written request of September 15.
The redelivery charge on the Watertown fasteners shipment is rated as due on the shipping desk's written instruction of September 17 to redeliver and bill it.
The redelivery charge on the Sioux City sealants shipment is claimed at $88 under section 6.1.
The inside delivery billed on the Superior gypsum board shipment is claimed at $60 under section 6.1.
The Superior roofing shipment appears on the claim schedule under section 4.6 for a discount rounded down on a half cent.
The freight bill whose pro number matches no bill of lading is rated against the bill of lading its ship date, state, weight and class identify.
The July freight bill for the Fergus Falls windows is reported as an undercharge of $95.
The undercharge list shows the July freight bill's ninety-day balance-due window closed on October 12.
The summary counts 20 freight bills with an exception.
The claim schedule carries the six items section 7.2 lists for each claimed freight bill.
The note tells the controller to confirm whether each void or withdrawn freight bill was paid before she files.
The note names the seven billed items the audit accepts on a document in the billing file or a written confirmation from the shipping desk.
The audit tab rates all 46 freight bills with a contract total beside the billed total.
The workbook wrongly nets the undercharges against the overcharges in the claim total although section 7.3 bars netting.
The workbook wrongly rates a fuel surcharge on the invoice-date week although section 5.2 keys the surcharge to the pickup date.
The workbook wrongly claims the first freight bill on a duplicated pro number although section 7.1 voids only the second.
The workbook wrongly applies the discount to accessorial charges although section 6.2 excludes them from it.
The workbook wrongly claims a fuel overcharge on a freight bill for a pickup in the week of September 21 although the tariff table gives 27.5 percent for that week's index.
The workbook wrongly rates the Bismarck liftgate as due although the shipping desk's word to bill it is dated the day after delivery.
The workbook wrongly includes the Williston gypsum board freight bill among its deficit-weight exceptions although the minimum charge leaves its amount due as billed.
The workbook wrongly leaves a second freight bill on an already billed pro number out of the exception count although section 7.1 voids it.
Overall formatting and style of the deliverable as an audit the controller can attach to the claim letter.
